name: Glutamine
short: No adverse effects in a placebo-controlled trial in older adults. A review says it can cause kidney damage in diabetic kidney disease; long-term safety data are limited.
text: In a double-blind placebo-controlled trial in older adults, oral glutamine did not significantly change any of the measures evaluated and no adverse effects were reported. A review found no significant adverse effects of glutamine supplementation taken for up to two weeks by healthy athletes, but stated that it can cause glomerulosclerosis and raised serum creatinine in the setting of diabetic kidney disease. An earlier safety review noted that very few studies had safety as a primary goal and that chronic use by healthy people of all age groups had not been fully taken into account. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
